sections.html:
The Recorder keeps Holmes County's land records at 75 E. Clinton Street, Suite 101, Millersburg, OH 44654. Phone (330) 674-5916, fax (330) 674-0782. Card, check or cash all work at the counter, deeds included.

Suite 101 holds these records:

  • deeds, mortgages and leases
  • liens for mechanics, workers' compensation, unemployment and federal taxes
  • partnerships, UCC financing statements and soldier's discharges
  • plats

Most sellers touch only two of these: the deed they sign and any mortgage release the lender files after payoff.

sections.h2: Why a Holmes County deed visits several offices first
sections.html:
Holmes County's conveyance standards, effective March 1, 2019, require a description review before the Auditor or Recorder sees the paper. Tax Map Office approval is mandatory for every legal description, plat, land contract, mineral deed and access easement.

Farm tracts that pass between families often carry old metes and bounds wording, and that is what the Tax Map staff read line by line. Budget one workday for each submission. The standards promise 24 hours between drop-off and pick-up, with longer waits for complex files. You can ask for an early review of a draft, which keeps the signed deed from bouncing.

sections.h2: Order of stops for a deed
sections.html:
The county's conveyance-by-mail sheet sets out four stops. Each has its own forms and fees, and mailed paper needs a stamped, pre-addressed envelope for every stop.

StepOfficeLocation and phoneWhat it does
1Tax Map Office75 E. Clinton St., Suite 102, (330) 674-6631Reviews the description, 24-hour period
2Planning Commission2 Court St., Suite 2, (330) 674-8625Stamps papers that need its approval
3County Auditor75 E. Clinton St., Suite 107Collects conveyance and transfer fees
4County Recorder75 E. Clinton St., Suite 101Records the deed

The Auditor looks for the Tax Map and Planning Commission stamps before touching a file, so a skipped stop freezes everything behind it.

sections.h2: What the Auditor collects from a seller
sections.html:
The county standards print $4.00 per thousand dollars of sale price as the conveyance fee and $0.50 for each parcel on the document as the transfer fee. Confirm both numbers with the Auditor before you set a closing date. State law assigns the bill to the grantor, meaning the seller (R.C. 319.202(D)).

  • Make the check payable to the Holmes County Auditor and send recording fees separately.
  • The office returns no change on an overpaid check and will not accept a signed blank check.
  • A check stopped on a transfer is referred to the county Prosecutor.
  • Attach form DTE 100, or DTE 100EX when the transfer qualifies for an exemption. Homestead property adds DTE 101 and current agricultural use land adds DTE 102.

Moving a mobile home title takes one more stamp. The Auditor will not process that transfer until the Treasurer's stamp shows the home's taxes are paid.

Most documents cost $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 per page after that, under R.C. 317.32 and 317.36. Senate Bill 94 amended the statute effective October 24, 2024, so a county may now add a preservation surcharge of as much as five dollars. Phone the office for the total on your page count.

Formatting can raise the bill. R.C. 317.114 sets the layout, and a paper that misses it is still recorded, for an extra $10.00 service charge plus a $10.00 housing trust fund charge. Before you print the deed, check these points:

  • type of 10 points or larger, in black or blue ink, with no highlighting
  • sheets between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches
  • a one inch margin at each side and the foot of every page
  • three blank inches at the head of page one, and an inch and a half on later pages

Court and taxing-authority papers, plats, DD-214s and state or federal documents are exempt.

Two search tools sit on the Recorder's page. AVA needs no login and fits a one-time lookup. Laredo Anywhere is for people who search often, and the county posts a setup guide in its document library. Both show images of deeds, easements, rights-of-way and leases. Other record types can be viewed from 1980 forward, and plats live on the Tax Map Department website.

The office accepts documents electronically, including deeds. It works with four vendors: ePN, Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services and CSC, which serve title companies, law firms and banks that record regularly. Most sellers never use this route directly, since the title company handles it at closing.

Owners can sign up for Property Fraud Alert through the Recorder, and a flyer sits in the Recorder section of the county document library. An alert matters most to an owner who lives away from the house or who has just inherited it, because a forged deed or an unexpected lien only shows up in the public record after it is filed.

Once a sale closes, the recorded deed is the buyer's proof of ownership. Check that it shows the correct parcel, the Tax Map Office stamp and the Auditor's endorsement before anything is handed over.

Holmes County had 44,970 residents in July 2025 and 14,592 housing units. Owners occupy 79.0% of homes, the middle owner-occupied home is worth $267,700 and median household income is $76,140. Calling or visiting Suites 101, 102 and 107 often beats an online form here, and the county's heavy Amish population makes farm and acreage sales a common part of the market.

sections.h2: Military discharges and a seller's checklist
sections.html:
Soldier's discharges are filed here, but they stay out of the public record for 75 years. Only authorized parties, such as the discharged service member, a county service officer or an heir of a deceased service member, can obtain one. Anyone else sees just name, rank, birth date, discharge date and type.

Here is a short checklist before you sell: get the legal description reviewed by the Tax Map Office, collect the Planning Commission stamp if it applies, pay the Auditor's fees with the right DTE form, then record. If a mortgage is being paid off, ask the lender when the release will be filed. If you plan to mail the packet instead of walking it between suites, call each office first and confirm the fee it will want, then enclose a separate check and envelope for each stop. Keep copies of every stamped page, since they show the order in which the offices handled the deed if a question comes up later.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Holmes County Recorder by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts cash, check and credit card, and the same applies to deeds and other conveyance documents.

faqs.q: Is Tax Map approval needed before a Holmes County deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Yes, whenever the paper carries a legal description. The standards route all descriptions, land contracts, mineral deeds and easements to the Tax Map Office first, with a 24-hour review.

faqs.q: Who owes the conveyance fee on a Holmes County sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. R.C. 319.202(D) charges the grantor, and the Auditor's schedule prints $4.00 per thousand dollars of price plus $0.50 per parcel. Verify the figures with the Auditor.

faqs.q: Can a Holmes County deed go through the mail?
faqs.a: Yes. Follow the four-stop sheet in order, and enclose forms, fees and a pre-addressed, correctly stamped envelope for each office.

faqs.q: Who can obtain a recorded military discharge in Holmes County?
faqs.a: Only authorized parties, such as the discharged service member, a county service officer or an heir of a deceased service member. A discharge stays out of the public record for 75 years.
